mitigation_candidates.evidence: MSRC describes a local Windows Update Stack privilege-elevation path; reducing untrusted local code execution may reduce exposure but does not remove the vulnerable component.
Detection and response may limit post-exploitation impact, but Microsoft does not document generic EDR as blocking the link-following path.
MSRC states that exploitation requires attacker-controlled code in a low-privilege AppContainer; restricting untrusted local execution can reduce opportunity but does not block ALPC.
Exploit prevention may detect heap-corruption behavior, but no vendor-specific control is documented as blocking this ALPC path.
The affected service is an identity control plane; stronger authentication may reduce account misuse but is not documented as blocking this elevation path.
Limiting administrative roles can reduce blast radius if privileges are elevated, but it is not an exact workaround.
Least-privilege service identities can limit the consequence of privilege elevation but do not block the service vulnerability.
Azure-managed service reachability is deployment-dependent and the MSRC record does not establish that customer network controls block this path.
Authentication controls are relevant to Entra ID risk, but MSRC does not state that MFA blocks this specific elevation path.
Privileged-role minimization limits impact from an Entra ID privilege elevation; it is not an exact workaround.
Filtering untrusted downloaded or emailed content can reduce delivery of malicious Shell content, but is not documented as fully blocking exploitation.
Application control can restrict untrusted payload execution after content delivery; it is not a documented Microsoft workaround.
The affected NFS service is network reachable; removing exposure to untrusted networks reduces reachability but does not remove the vulnerable driver.
Restricting NFS clients to approved networks reduces reachable attackers while the driver remains vulnerable for allowed clients.
NFS is a network service; removing untrusted network exposure reduces reachability without eliminating vulnerable code.
Restricting NFS client networks limits potential senders while preserving required service access.
SSTP can be externally reachable in VPN deployments; removing unnecessary Internet exposure reduces reachable attack paths.
Restricting SSTP access to approved peers limits reachability but does not correct the protocol implementation.
RRAS is a network-facing service; removing unnecessary external reachability reduces exposure but is not a vendor workaround.
Network ACLs can limit RRAS clients to approved segments, reducing reachable attackers.
Restricting Netlogon and RPC reachability to domain-trusted networks reduces exposure while preserving required identity services.
Netlogon protocol hardening may reduce abuse of legacy paths, but no exact Microsoft workaround is asserted.
Restricting Message Queuing from untrusted networks reduces network reachability but does not remove the vulnerable service.
The reviewed MSRC record does not establish an explicit service-disable workaround, so no path-blocking credit is assigned.
Filtering untrusted image files reduces delivery of crafted content but is not an exact Microsoft workaround.
Application control can constrain post-exploitation payload execution but receives no exploit-likelihood credit because the relationship is generic.
Limiting HTTP Print Provider exposure reduces network reachability but does not patch the provider.
Restricting print-provider traffic to trusted print infrastructure reduces reachable attackers.
Filtering crafted graphics files reduces likely content-delivery paths; it is not an exact vendor workaround.
Protected View may help if the parser is reached through Office, but the MSRC record does not establish that relationship.
Restricting recursive or authoritative DNS exposure to intended clients reduces network reachability.
DNS ACLs and segmentation limit which sources can send requests to the vulnerable service but do not correct DNS Server code.
DHCP should be reachable only from intended network segments; ACLs reduce untrusted request reachability.
Keeping DHCP away from untrusted network boundaries reduces attack surface without claiming to block the flaw.
DHCP ACLs and network segmentation limit which clients can reach the service.
Keeping DHCP off untrusted networks reduces reachable attack sources but does not patch the service.
Limiting externally reachable Skype for Business endpoints reduces attack surface for a network RCE.
Restricting signaling and service access to trusted segments reduces reachable attackers but does not remove vulnerable code.
Opening untrusted Word documents in Protected View can reduce active-content execution, but Microsoft does not state that it blocks this CVE.
Filtering malicious document attachments and downloads reduces delivery likelihood without claiming exact-path blocking.
Mail filtering can reduce delivery of malicious Outlook content, but the MSRC record does not establish a complete workaround.
Protected View may reduce risk for downloaded Office content; applicability to Outlook's exact trigger is not established.
Cluster communications should be restricted to cluster members and management networks, reducing reachable attack sources.
Removing cluster protocols from untrusted networks reduces attack surface; no exact MSRC workaround is claimed.
Disabling Internet Connection Sharing could remove the service, but the MSRC record does not provide an explicit vendor disablement instruction for this CVE.
Restricting related traffic to trusted segments reduces reachability but is not a patch.
Restricting SQL Server administrative and service privileges limits consequences of elevation but does not block the vulnerable authorization path.
Restricting SQL management and database protocols to approved networks reduces reachable attackers.
Limiting Copilot Studio administrative roles reduces the consequence of privilege elevation but is not an exact workaround.
Strong authentication protects identities used with Copilot Studio, but the MSRC record does not establish it as a blocker for this flaw.
